title: Fix `TextEdit` scrolling too far vertically
body:
## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

Fixes many scrolling related issues:

- Fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/123577
- Supersedes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/123605
- Fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/95629
- Fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/49941 (duplicate?)

Disabling `scroll_past_end_of_file` when past the end of file did not immediately update the scroll in some cases.

Toggling word wrap when at the end of text did not update the scroll immediately and causes it to jump when next updated.

Increasing the height of a TextEdit kept the same first visible line, even if it caused it to scroll past the end of file (when it wasn't enabled), until the entire text can be seen. 
In 4.7.2 it worked, but it always jumped to a whole line, instead of smoothly scrolling to fit the text.

Resizing the TextEdit always scrolled to fully show the first visible line. Even when the height didn't change. It's fine to leave a line part way scrolled down, I don't think it was intentional.

Removing lines when scrolled to the last line when the TextEdit is not visible caused it to scroll past the last line.

Resizing the TextEdit with word wrapping enabled near the end of the text could cause the first visible line to change, such as shrinking the width quickly. This was because `_update_wrap_at_column` called `set_line_as_first_visible` using outdated values, the line wrap counts of the text were updated but the scroll maximum wasn't updated to account for them.

`set_line_as_last_visible` did not fully scroll to a line if the TextEdit could perfectly fit a whole number of lines. This is because `_get_visible_lines_offset` clamped to `.999`.
`get_last_full_visible_line` was returning the line before the last fully visible line some cases, like when the scroll was not at a whole line.
The test cases were even checking for this, they called `set_line_as_last_visible` with a line and checked that the last visible line was the line before that.

When showing the horizontal scrollbar causes the vertical scrollbar to show, it relies on `_update_scrollbars` being called a second time from the draw call to update it.
 
When the height was smaller than a single line, the max scroll was limited to not reach the end of the last line. Both with and without `scroll_past_end_of_file_enabled`.

`scroll_past_end_of_file` stopped at 2 lines before the end instead of the last line, if the height didn't exactly fit a whole number of lines.


Fixes scrolling test case issues:

Some test checks were not functional. For example, `CHECK(Math::is_equal_approx(text_edit->get_v_scroll(), double((visible_lines * 4))) + 6);`, the `+ 6` is outside of the parenthesis so it was doing `false + 6` which always evaluates to `true`. In most cases, if the addition was in the correct parenthesis it would pass, but not for all of them.

No subcases were used for these tests for performance reasons, but there has been performance improvements recently so its not that slow, and the reason it was slow in the first place was the way it was setting up the TextEdit was very inefficient by adding one line at a time to the first line. 
Average CPU time of running `--test --tc="*[TextEdit] viewport"`
master 0.168s
PR 0.106
I added subcases and optimized the setup. (use ignore whitespace to see what actually changed in the tests).

An arbitrary height was used, making it dependent on the theme size. What is important is the number of visible lines it shows.

The last visible line wrap index was being used, but not the first visible line wrap index. This is relevant for tests since `set_line_as_first_visible` takes a wrap index.
I don't know why its not exposed compared to the last visible line wrap index, but I didn't expose it here.

## Additional information

I was only trying to fix one issue but this is a rabbit hole of connected problems. There are even more that I'll make more PRs for.

`first_visible_line` and similar now are only set when the scrollbar updates. This should help prevent it from getting desynced.
The method that gets the height of the text area was losing precision in some calculations by making it an int too early.
I also made `content_size_cache` not use ints for size.
I split `_scroll_moved` into 2 functions, usually only one scroll is updated at a time.
I simplified the `first_visible_line` calculation by handling placeholders and no wrapping separately. Following the logic, it should be the same.

Some more test changes
- Added scroll checks when the word wrapping is toggled on and off for multiple subcases.
- Added `set_line_as_last_visible` checks for setting it to a line that can't be last and to the actual last line.
- Added horizontal auto adjust tests, which was a todo. These are very simple, since h scroll uses pixels so it would be more complex to calculate and probably not as helpful. There is no corresponding get first visible character method either. They just check if the caret is visible, and if the scroll is 0 or not, which should still be useful.
- Added test to make sure resizing keeps the first visible line.
- The vertical adjust tests now use the fact there are an exact number of lines, so the expected first visible lines have changed.
- When checks use Math::floor, it can just use ints instead of `is_equal_approx`.
